bread.name: Bread
bread.intro: Breads ranked by nutrient density per 100 calories using the NRF9.3 score, with sodium as an extra tiebreaker. Whole-grain and sprouted breads lead because they keep the fiber, magnesium and B vitamins that refining removes.

cereal.name: Breakfast cereal
cereal.intro: Ready-to-eat cereals ranked by nutrient density per 100 calories (NRF9.3), with sugar as the tiebreaker. Fortification adds vitamins and iron to many cereals, so high fiber and low sugar separate the genuinely healthy ones.

cheese.name: Cheese
cheese.exclude: spread|sauce|substitute|imitation|food|product|pasteurized process|fondue|puffs|dry|powder|nonfat|fat free|low fat|lowfat|reduced fat|low sodium|with vegetables|caraway|pimento|tilsit|limburger|port de salut|romano|queso|mexican|goat, hard|goat, semisoft|ricotta, part|cream, fat|whey
cheese.intro: Cheeses ranked per ounce by nutrient density (NRF9.3 per 100 calories), with sodium and saturated fat as tiebreakers. Fresh and soft cheeses score well on calories; hard aged cheeses deliver the most protein and calcium per ounce.

fast-food.name: Fast food
fast-food.exclude: School Lunch|^Fast foods, (shrimp|clams)|sundae|cookie|brownie|pie|cake|danish|cinnamon|croissant|biscuit, with|hushpuppies|onion rings|french fries|potato, french|hash|nachos|frijoles|coleslaw|salad, vegetable|salad, with|dessert|milk shake|soda|cola|chips|crispy|crust
fast-food.intro: Fast-food meals, sandwiches and entrées from the USDA database ranked by nutrient density per 100 calories (NRF9.3), with sodium and saturated fat as tiebreakers. Grilled chicken, bean and egg items rise to the top; fried and cheese-heavy items sink.

energy-drinks.name: Energy drink
energy-drinks.intro: Energy drinks ranked per 8 fl oz on the two things that matter most for a daily habit: sugar and calories, with caffeine shown so you can judge the dose. Sugar-free versions dominate the top; a regular can of most brands carries 25 to 30 g of sugar.

protein-bars.name: Protein and granola bar
protein-bars.intro: Protein, energy and granola bars ranked by nutrient density per 100 calories (NRF9.3) with sugar and saturated fat as tiebreakers. Bars built on nuts, oats and added protein lead; chocolate-coated and marshmallow bars trail.

milk.name: Milk
milk.include: ^Milk, (whole|reduced fat|lowfat|nonfat|fluid)|^Beverages, (almond milk|rice milk|coconut milk|oat)|^Soymilk|^Milk, goat|^Milk, sheep
milk.exclude: dry|evaporated|condensed|chocolate|without added vitamin|with added nonfat milk solids|protein fortified|calcium fortified|(?<!un)sweetened|chai|nog|flavor|human|SILK|Beverages, coconut milk, sweetened
milk.intro: Dairy and plant milks ranked per cup by nutrient density per 100 calories (NRF9.3), with sugar and saturated fat as tiebreakers. Skim and low-fat dairy and fortified soy milk lead on protein and calcium per calorie; unsweetened almond milk is lowest in calories but also in protein.

fruits.name: Fruit
fruits.intro: Fresh fruits ranked by nutrient density per 100 calories (NRF9.3). Berries, citrus and melons score highest because they pack vitamin C, potassium and fiber into few calories; dense sweet fruits like dates and bananas rank lower per calorie but remain good potassium sources.

vegetables.name: Vegetable
vegetables.intro: Vegetables ranked by nutrient density per 100 calories (NRF9.3). Dark leafy greens dominate: they deliver vitamins A, C and K, calcium, iron, magnesium and potassium for almost no calories.

nuts.name: Nuts and seeds
nuts.intro: Nuts and seeds ranked per ounce by nutrient density per 100 calories (NRF9.3). All are calorie-dense, so the ranking rewards those with the most protein, fiber, magnesium, iron and vitamin E per calorie: pumpkin seeds, chia, flax, sunflower seeds and almonds.
